podcast.body: This song served as the first single from "A Moon-Shaped Pool." Its title phrase had appeared on the 2003 album "Hail to the Thief," suggesting a long development period. Tragically, the string section for "Burn the Witch" was recorded on the day that longtime producer Nigel Godrich's father passed away. The video for the song later faced accusations of copyright infringement due to its distinct visual style. "And this time, it's the first single from a Munchet pool here's Burn the Witch."

podcast.body: This song, released as the first single from Radiohead's "A Moon Shaped Pool" album, has a unique origin story: it was conceived, composed, and partially recorded many years earlier during the extensive and creatively explosive sessions for the "Kid A" album. This demonstrates the profound and lasting impact of the "Kid A" recording period, which continues to supply material for the band's modern releases. "Fue pensado, fue compuesto y fue parcialmente grabado durante las grabaciones del quidá."
